Sera — concise description for AI explanation

Sera is a student-first mobile app that brings a whole school together in one place: schedules, class chats, clubs, and a school-wide feed. It is designed and operated by students for students, prioritizing simple social coordination and daily school life rather than administrative or classroom management.

Core idea
- Tagline: "Your school, all in one place." Sera centralizes what students already care about: class schedules, period times, short messages to groups, and event announcements.

Primary user-facing features (high level)
- Onboarding: a short, guided signup that collects a display name, username, school, grade, and basic preferences.
- Schedule & classes: students add or scan their class schedules; the app uses an AI-assisted scanner to match classes with bell times and create class rooms automatically.
- Class rooms & clubs: lightweight group chats scoped to classes or clubs, created from schedule input or student actions.
- School feed: a single, school-wide feed for posts and threaded replies so announcements and conversations are public to the school community.
- Bell schedule voting: students can vote on daily schedule types (e.g., regular, early release) and the majority choice controls that day's period times.

Product principles & constraints
- Student-led: there are no teacher or administrator account types — the platform is intentionally peer-run.
- No private DMs: communication is always community- or group-scoped (no one-to-one direct messages).
- No anonymity: every post and message is tied to a real account to keep accountability.
- No gradebook or official school data integration: Sera is not a substitute for district systems and never imports official student records.
- No ads or data selling: the product avoids monetization that would trade off student privacy.

Privacy & compliance note
- The design deliberately minimizes sensitive data collection and avoids becoming a technology provider to districts; privacy safeguards and tightened Firestore rules are required before any public rollout.

Tone, audience, and UX expectations
- Audience: primarily high-school students who want a simple social hub for class coordination and school life.
- Tone: casual, concise, and school-centric — content and UX should be fast to read and act on (quick posts, short messages, clear schedules).

What to emphasize when explaining Sera
- Focus on the human problem: Sera replaces fragmented student tools with one place for schedules, group chats, events, and school announcements.
- Highlight the social design choices: student-run, public-by-default (within a school), no DMs, and accountability through non-anonymous posting.
- Note the AI-assisted convenience: the schedule scanner reduces the friction of adding classes and bell times, making setup fast for students.

Status snapshot
- Sera is positioned as a student-focused MVP with core flows implemented; remaining operational items (push notifications, production media storage, and security rule hardening) are part of launch readiness.

If you need a short explanation to present to a user or stakeholder
- "Sera is a student-run mobile app that centralizes schedules, class chats, clubs, and a school feed so students can organize their day and school community in one place — simple, public-by-school, and privacy-minded."

Last updated: April 2026
